html:
The Musket Wars were a series of wars among Māori tribes in the early 19th century, after some groups got muskets from European traders. Thousands died and whole peoples were driven from their land.

The Ngāpuhi chief Hongi Hika, of the Bay of Islands, visited England in 1820, came back with guns, and led raids deep into the North Island. Others armed themselves in turn, and raids reached the Chatham Islands, where the Moriori were enslaved.

The wars ended as all sides had guns. They changed tribal boundaries and weakened Māori before the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840. See Ka Mate, composed by Te Rauparaha.
